title: Graceful Diversion Timeline — prototype for staged traffic diversions and rollback briefing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Short summary: Design a timeline-first UI for Redwood Console rollouts that focuses on graceful diversions — staged traffic shifts to fallback variants or regions, with explicit pause points and rollback briefings. The prototype emphasizes a chronological 'diversion lane' for canary and A/B experiments, visualizing coverage, signal thresholds, and cost/latency estimates.
background: We need a clearer way to manage staged rollouts where operators can divert traffic gradually across models, regions, or capacity tiers and immediately see the operational impact. Existing split UI is modal and not expressive enough for complex multi-stage diversions (eg diversion to fallback cluster + partial shadowing). PM asks for a timeline that surfaces safety gates, automated pause conditions, and quick rollback affordances.
design_goals: Make staged diversions readable within a single timeline
Surface primary signals (latency, error rate, quality regressions, cost delta) inline with each stage
Allow quick manual interventions (pause, accelerate, rollback) without losing context
Preserve auditability (decision reason + snapshot) for compliance
Accessible interactions: keyboard-first controls and clear color contrast
user_flows: Create new diversion: choose baseline and target variants, then author N stages with target percentages and duration windows
Run: timeline animates as stages progress; primary signal graphs update under each stage; can attach reason for advancing/pausing
Emergency rollback: one-click deploy snapback from any stage with optional staged rollback plan
Post-mortem: export timeline with metric snapshots and operator notes
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates creating a 3-stage diversion with per-stage guards
Timeline shows inline latency/error/cost sparkline for each stage
Operator can pause/resume stage and capture a required reason
Rollback button triggers a confirm modal with suggested rollback path and impact estimate
Design includes keyboard-accessible controls and color-blind safe palettes
risks_and_tradeoffs: Adding a timeline increases surface complexity — may overwhelm novice users; mitigate with 'simple mode' presets
Inline metrics risk clutter — we use progressive disclosure (sparklines + expand)
Calculating cost delta for arbitrary stage windows requires backend support (ENG dependency)
engineering_notes: Requires rollout state machine changes for staged diversion checkpoints: ENG-7903
Backwards compatibility with existing traffic-split API must be preserved; plan includes a compatibility shim
reviews_and_feedback: PM review (Noah Sullivan) 2026-02-25: wants clearer default guard suggestions and integration with Optimize recommendations
Eng review (Priya Rao) 2026-02-27: asked for avoidance of synchronous metric pulls on stage transitions; prefer evented updates
Security 2026-02-28: audit log requirements OK but request explicit 'export snapshot' permission scope
Design review 2026-02-26 (Cross-team): suggested adding a 'test shadow' toggle for non-intrusive validation
usability_testing: Session 1 (synthetic infra team): participants completed staged rollout creation in 8m avg; confusion point: selecting fallback variant ordinally vs by region
Session 2 (platform PMs): participants wanted clearer estimate of user-visible impact during partial diversions
next_steps: Refine default guard templates (latency + p50/p95 + error rate + quality delta)
Hand off for API contract for metric snapshots (ENG-7821) and rollout checkpoints (ENG-7903)
Accessibility pass: keyboard flow and ARIA labels
Prototype iteration addressing PM feedback re: Optimize integration

final_note: Aim for a lightweight, timeline-native UX that scales from simple two-stage canaries to multi-stage diversion strategies used by enterprise customers. This prototype is intentionally conservative in visual density to reduce cognitive load while preserving rich guardrails for power users.
